resources.string: This router has not provided a verified policy for this phone. No DNS or captain permissions are inferred from the old global Mast response.
No verified DNS policy has been received for this phone.
Android is not using the hostname in the verified policy.
The selected provider matches, but protection against editing has not been verified.
Android did not apply DNS protection

Android only accepts a DNS-over-TLS resolver it can reach right now, and it could not. Until it can, the phone keeps its earlier DNS setting, so filtering may not apply. FamilyWarden keeps trying and never chooses an unfiltered fallback itself.
Checking for a DNS answer over a verified TLS connection.
DNS certificate could not be verified
The hostname, certificate chain, expiry, or device clock may be wrong. There is no skip-verification option.
Possible causes include a resolver outage, an access restriction, blocked port 853, or a network login page. Strict DNS stays configured; there is no unfiltered fallback.
TLS worked, but the test did not receive a usable DNS response. This does not establish which component failed.
The last test answered over TLS. This confirms the resolver path, not every filtering category or application.
DNS is applied; connection not tested
Android\'s strict DNS setting is locked. Test this network to check resolver reachability.
This phone\'s signed policy could not be confirmed. Sync with the router; an unknown state is not evidence of protection.
Waiting for this phone\'s signed policy
Router out of reach; cached policy remains
Reply could not be verified; last trusted policy retained
Sync failed; last trusted policy retained
DNS filters domains, not individual page contents. Apps with their own DNS or a VPN may bypass system DNS. Hotspot clients are not covered by this status.
Once applied, DNS protection stays on while paired, independently of Ulysses. No automatic unfiltered fallback.
Sail home: end the pact early
Opens the router\'s sail page in the browser: the router password and the line from the song, then the waiting period before the pact ends. Needs a route to your router, normally home Wi-Fi or a VPN.
Optional hotspot self-binding. Does not turn DNS protection on or off.
Only a router-confirmed captain can enable Ulysses.
The router confirms that this phone belongs to the captain profile. During an active pact, hotspot follows its schedule and this feature cannot be turned off.
Removal requires explicit administrator authorization. No active pact alone is not permission.
An applicable pact is still active. Use the router\'s supported release process; this dialog cannot bypass it.
This phone is not authorized for self-removal. Managed-device removal requires explicit administrator approval.
The router could not be reached. Cached state is not fresh removal permission. Reconnect through home Wi-Fi or a VPN.
The router did not provide device-specific authorization. A global Mast reply cannot authorize removal of this enrolled device.
A fresh response for this phone could not be verified. The last trusted policy remains; check the router connection and paired key.
Removal was not completed. Check the current device-owner state and try again when authorized.
This installation is not provisioned yet. Removing it relinquishes Device Owner rights; future enrollment may require account/profile changes or a reset.

FamilyWarden will check authorization again, set Private DNS back to Automatic, clear its own restrictions, and give up Device Owner rights. Android can\'t restore an earlier \"Off\" setting exactly. Enrollment later may require account/profile changes or a reset.
This requires a verified device-specific policy from a compatible router.
Pairing could not be completed. Check the address, connectivity, and key fingerprint.
The connection can be tested once Android has applied and locked the DNS setting.
Ask the administrator to approve this phone in LuCI under FamilyWarden › Phones. The fingerprint there must match this one:
The router no longer approves this phone; last policy kept
If another Device Owner, including the older Mast app, already manages this phone, stop here. Do not remove it, delete accounts, or reset the phone without an approved migration.
